dedupe_keys.name: data and code for exploiting multi objective reinforcement learning and explainable artificial intelligence to navigate robust regional water supply investment pathways

description: The TRAILS authors publish code for multi-objective reinforcement-learning analysis of regional water-supply investments. Zenodo archives release 1.0 under a BSD-2-Clause-NetBSD metadata label and links a public GitHub repository that identifies BSD 2-Clause. The documented application concerns six cooperating utilities in North Carolina Research Triangle through 2060. The workflow evaluates adaptive infrastructure pathways, utility-specific reliability and cost, and time-varying robustness under hydrologic and demand uncertainty. It uses explainable analysis to identify drivers of conflict between utility preferences. This model can test investment and operating choices in multi-utility supply simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this TRAILS release. Coverage is the six-utility case and its scenario assumptions, not every regional institution. A limitation is that learned policies depend on reward, uncertainty and state definitions; reported robustness does not establish political agreement. The code was not compiled or run and costs were not independently checked.
